trigger: Continuation of single-asset-evidence-ledger-09/-10.json's search for the negative-reserve single-asset gap. This batch first checked 9 more already-in-pool, universe-PASS, negative-labeled candidates that still had single_asset_status=PENDING (ONTX, IDRA, APTX, ANAB x2, OMER, ICPT, REPH, APLT), following the same qualification discipline (pre-event 10-K/10-Q 'Item 1. Business' overview; count only a company whose pre-event filings show one meaningful active clinical-stage therapeutic asset). All 9 were DOES_NOT_QUALIFY, each with an explicitly named second active compound - a similarly low yield to the earlier ledgers. Rather than continuing to check already-in-pool candidates essentially at random, pivoted to EDGAR full-text search for the literal phrase 'our only product candidate' in 10-Ks, which directly surfaces self-declared single-asset companies. Cross-referencing against real negative catalysts found two genuine QUALIFIES candidates not previously in the pool (Tricida/veverimer and Aerovate/AV-101, sourced in newly-sourced-batch-14.json), each with an explicit 'our only product candidate' pre-event 10-K statement - a stronger evidentiary bar than the inference-from-silence pattern used for SGTX/MDGL.

meaningful_active_therapeutic_assets: two other clinical-stage product candidates (unnamed in the overview)
rows.evidence_summary: FY2019 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview states: 'We have one Phase 3 clinical-stage product candidate and two other clinical-stage product candidates (one of which has been studied for treatment of acute radiation syndromes) and preclinical programs' - an explicit disclosure of at least three active clinical-stage candidates beyond rigosertib being the lead.

FY2017 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview names two lead drug candidates: 'Our TLR agonist lead drug candidate IMO-2125...Our TLR antagonist lead drug candidate is IMO-8400.' IMO-2125 was in active combination development with checkpoint inhibitors (ipilimumab, pembrolizumab) for melanoma at the same time IMO-8400 was in development for dermatomyositis - two separate, equally active named programs.

No 10-K existed pre-event (IPO'd June 2018); the most recent pre-event periodic filing, the Q3 2018 10-Q, names three distinct product candidates in active clinical development: NYX-2925 (two Phase 2 studies, chronic pain), NYX-783 (Phase 1 complete, PTSD Phase 2 planned), and NYX-458 (Phase 1 ongoing, Parkinson's cognitive impairment).

FY2020 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview: 'Our most advanced wholly-owned antibody programs, imsidolimab, ANB030 and ANB032, are designed to modulate therapeutic targets that are genetically associated with human inflammatory disorders' - three named, equally-described active programs.

FY2023 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview names two wholly-owned checkpoint agonists in clinical development (rosnilimab, ANB032), two cytokine antagonists being explored for out-licensing (imsidolimab in Phase 3, etokimab Phase 2/3-ready), and two additional preclinical candidates (ANB033, ANB101) - by far the most diversified pipeline of any candidate checked in this batch.

FY2020 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview describes a marketed product (OMIDRIA), narsoplimab under BLA priority review, an active Phase 1 MASP-3 inhibitor program (OMS906), a completed Phase 1 PDE7 addiction program, and a diverse group of preclinical programs including GPR174 - a diversified commercial-stage company, not a single-asset issuer.

FY2019 10-K names INT-787, an FXR agonist with pharmacological properties distinct from OCA, as a compound 'we are currently evaluating in preclinical studies' - an actively-evaluated second candidate, not merely a discontinued or backup compound (a separate compound, INT-767, is explicitly described in the same filing as no longer actively developed, and does not itself disqualify).

FY2017 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview: 'Our pipeline also includes other early-stage product candidates, including Dex-IN, a proprietary intranasal formulation of dexmedetomidine' - a second named therapeutic candidate. (The separate CDMO manufacturing division is a revenue-generating service business, not a competing therapeutic asset, and would not by itself have disqualified the company.)

meaningful_active_therapeutic_assets: two other AR-program small molecules (AT-001, AT-002)
rows.evidence_summary: FY2023 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview: 'Our AR program currently includes three small molecules, which are all potent and selective inhibitors of AR, but are engineered to have unique tissue permeability profiles to target different disease states' - govorestat plus two other named active AR-inhibitor compounds targeting diabetic complications and heart disease.

FY2019 10-K explicitly and repeatedly describes 'the prospects of veverimer (also known as TRC101), our only product candidate, which is still in development' - a direct self-declaration of single-asset status, stronger evidentially than the inference-from-silence pattern used to qualify SGTX and MDGL. Sourced via EDGAR full-text search for the literal phrase 'our only product candidate'.

FY2023 10-K states: 'Our business is entirely dependent on the successful development, regulatory approval and commercialization of AV-101, our only product candidate under development.' A direct self-declaration of single-asset status. Sourced via the same EDGAR full-text search as TCDA.

promotion_boundary: Single-asset status alone does not establish final M7 eligibility. Historical universe (already confirmed for TCDA and AVTE in historical-universe-ledger-46.json), timestamp, financing, point-in-time evidence, concentration, eligible-registry and deterministic cohort-freeze checks remain mandatory. This batch adds 2 new genuine QUALIFIES candidates to the pool, moving the pool-wide single-asset PASS count from 21 toward 23; per newly-sourced-batch-13.json's RNG order-sensitivity finding, the exact effect on any particular simulated selected-cohort subset is not a reliable pre-registry prediction.
